chunks: We were told by Ahmad bin Hasan al-Qattan, that he said: We were told by Abdul-Rahman bin Muhammad al-Hussaini, that he said: We were informed by Abu Ja'far Ahmad bin Isa bin Abi Maryam al-'Ajali, that he said: We were told by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Ziyad al-'Azrami, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hatim al-Manqari, of Mufaddal bin Umar, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Throne and the Chair: What are they?

He said: The Throne is, on one side, the totality of the creation, and the Chair is its vessel, and on the side of the last part of the Throne is the knowledge which Allah made His Prophets, Messengers and Proofs sight upon, and the Chair is the knowledge which Allah did not make anyone of His Prophets, Messengers and Proofs, peace be upon them, sight upon.

key_terms.أَنْبِيَاءَهُ وَرُسُلَهُ وَحُجَّجَهُ: His Prophets, Messengers, and Proofs, referring to the infallible figures granted divine insight.
key_terms.الْخَلْق: Creation, the totality of all created beings.
key_terms.الْعَرْش: The Throne, interpreted here as either the totality of creation or supreme divine knowledge.
key_terms.الْعِلْم: Knowledge, specifically divine knowledge in this context.
key_terms.الْكَرْسِيُّ: The Chair, interpreted as the vessel of creation or exclusive divine knowledge.
key_terms.وَاع: Vessel or container, describing the relationship of the Chair to the Throne.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Throne and the Chair in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this dual interpretation (zahir and batin) to reconcile physical cosmology with metaphysical epistemology, a hallmark of Shia hadith scholarship. The distinction highlights the hierarchy of divine revelation, where the 'Throne' of knowledge is accessible to the infallible Imams (Hujjah), while the 'Chair' denotes the esoteric depths of divine reality reserved exclusively for God, emphasizing the unique spiritual station of the Ahl al-Bayt.
